November 2009 # **9****th** **- 20****th** **November 2009** # **Codelco settles 2010 premium for China at $85/t** Codelco has settled its copper premium for delivery to China at $85/t for the 2010 annual contract. The premium is at the higher end of market expectations, which were around $80-$85/t. Against a background of a negative SHFE-LME arbitrage and a copper price which is surging to a new high for the year, consumers may feel reluctant to accept Codelco’s premium. Annual copper premium negotiations between consumers and other suppliers have just begun after the emergence of this benchmark. The uncertainty of the copper market outlook in 2010 has left consumers uncertain as to the amount they wish to purchase under contract. Until now they just waited for quotations from traders such as Trafigara, Wanxiang group and Maike group. Usually their quotations are lower than Codelco’s. If these traders also increase premiums by 13%, as Codelco has done, then their premium quotations may be around $73/t. Some traders worry that the current negative arbitrage between SHFE and LME could continue for some time, due to the large level of invisible stocks in China and the record high level of domestic cathode output. It looks unlikely that the market in 2010 will face the same issues of scrap shortage and buying activity by the SRB that it faced this year. Therefore, we find it difficult to imagine a prolonged positive arbitrage developing in China in the next few months. SHFE/LME 3-month price ratio

The spot premium for imported copper cathode is now $40-70/t. The premium for imported SXEW cathode is quoted at $40-50/t. However, we believe that actual deals are being done at nearer to $30-40/t, and quotations for copper premiums for bonded warehouse material may be lower still at about $20/t. A major reason for this appears to be that at the end of year some traders want to turn paper profits from the rise of the copper price into money in the bank. ## **Spot premium for imported cathode levels off at a low level** $/t

Data: CRU # **October cathodes imports fall** According to preliminary customs data, China imported 263,109t of unwrought copper and copper semis in October, down 34.1% m-o-m. After September’s surprisingly high copper import figure the October data is more in accordanc

e with the estimation of most market participants, and has not had a negative impact on prices. The reduced imports have occurred against a background of rising stocks. SHFE stocks have continued to build, rising 2.3% to 107,939t in the week ending 20th November. Furthermore, we believe that there are in the region of 150,000-200,000t of cathode in Shanghai bonded warehouses, with speculators holding a further 200,000-300,000t. The lower level of imports also reflects record domestic production; according to the NBS October cathode output reached 399,300t, up 1% m-o-m. Higher refined production may be due to the easing of copper scrap and blister supply. In addition, some smelters are keen to meet their annual production goals, so they are ramping up production before the end of 2009. Furthermore, as consumers near the end of 2009 they have become more cautious, particularly as the price has risen to nearly RMB 54,000/t. Therefore we believe that monthly cathode imports are likely to remain subdued in the remainder of 2009 compared to the record levels seen earlier in the year. # **Cathode re-export may increase further in the near future** Due to the high copper price restraining domestic copper consumption growth, stocks have risen in both bonded warehouses and on the SHFE exchange. With plentiful stocks and low premiums, some traders may want to reexport copper. Monthly exports of refined copper have already risen from almost nothing to more than 10,000t in September. Directly or indirectly, re-exports are likely to cause an increase in LME copper inventory, particularly in Asian warehouses. Chinese expSHFE inventoryts ofheads higher (000t)refined copper pick

Whilst few copper smelters told CRU that they are prepared to do copper concentrate tolling and export cathodes thus taking advantage of the small negative arbitrage between SHFE and LME, market sources said that Tongling Copper may have exported 5,000-6,000t of cathode in October. # **LME copper price surging, SHFE struggles to keep pace** Due to a weaker US dollar and an increasingly bullish view on the macro economy, LME copper prices jumped to a new high for the year of $6,990/t. Consequently, the SHFE 3-month copper price climbed to RMB 53,940/t on 18th November, whilst the cash to 3-month contango moved to RMB325/t. Chinese consumers are becoming more cautious about purchases with the price at current levels, especially given the growth in domestic supply. We emphasise that Chinese consumption has limited scope to increa

se quarter-on-quarter in Q4, moreover the higher copper price will restrain demand growth. As the LME copper price shows little sign of reversing its recent strength, the SHFE may struggle to find the energy to chase after it if it makes a convincing break above $7,000/t, at least for now. ### **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Grace Qu (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2206, ext. 321 grace.qu@crugroup.com **John Tomlinson (London):** +44 20 7903 2103 john.tomlinson@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 20th November 2009.
